nahhas-irab:19-19.t: إِنَّا أَرْسَلْنا عَلَيْهِمْ رِيحاً صَرْصَراً: The people of tafsīr (Quranic exegesis) say: الصّرصر is the cold [wind]. Some of the people of language said: it is only called صرصر when it has a violent sound, from their saying صرّ الشيء when a thing makes a sound; the origin is صرر, and one of the rāʾs was replaced by a ṣād. فِي يَوْمِ نَحْسٍ مُسْتَمِرٍّ: Some of the people of tafsīr said: النحس means "severe". Had it been as he said, يوم would have taken tanwīn (nunation) and it would have been said نحس [as an adjective], not in a genitive construct.

nahhas-irab:20-20.t:
تَنْزِعُ النَّاسَ: It was said: it plucked them out of the pits which they had dug. كَأَنَّهُمْ أَعْجازُ نَخْلٍ مُنْقَعِرٍ: النخل (palm trees) is treated as masculine and as feminine; these are two dialects, and the Qur'an has brought both. Muḥammad ibn Jarīr [al-Ṭabarī] claimed that there is an ellipsis in the wording and that the meaning is: "it plucks people out and leaves them like the trunks of palm trees." He said: on this view the kāf would be in the position of the accusative (naṣb) by the omitted verb. But this does not need the ellipsis he spoke of. The correct view on it is what Abū Isḥāq [al-Zajjāj] said; he said: it is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. it plucks people out [while they are] like palm trees uprooted, i.e. in this state. Abū Jaʿfar said: This view is the true i'rab; if one takes the meaning loosely, then the meaning comes back to what Muḥammad ibn Jarīr said.

Muḥammad ibn Isḥāq related: When the wind rose, a group of seven men of ʿĀd stood up, lined up at the entrance of the ravine, and blocked the wind from the women and children who were in the ravine. The wind then came in from underneath them one by one, uprooted each, turned him over onto his head and broke his neck, until it had destroyed six, and one remained, called al-Khaljān. He came to Hūd ﷺ and said: "What are these that I see like Bactrian camels beneath the clouds?" He said: "These are the angels, peace be upon them." He said: "If I accept Islam, what do I get?" He said: "You will be safe." He said: "Will your Lord grant me retaliation against those who are in the clouds?" He said: "Woe to you! Have you ever seen a king grant retaliation against his own troops?" He said: "Even if He did, I would not be content." He [the narrator] said: So he went back to his place and began to recite: [rajaz metre] 443-
لم يبق إلّا الخلجان نفسه ... يا شرّ يوم قد دهاني أمسه
(None is left but al-Khaljān himself; O worst of days, whose evening has struck me!)
Then there befell him what had befallen his companions, and they became as He, Majestic and Mighty, said: كَأَنَّهُمْ أَعْجازُ نَخْلٍ مُنْقَعِرٍ.

Mujāhid said about their being likened to the trunks of uprooted palm trees: it is because their bodies had been separated from their heads, so they became bodies without heads. One of the people of speculative reasoning said: the comparison is to the pits in which they had been standing; the pits became like the trunks of palm trees. Abū Jaʿfar said: This view is an erroneous one. Had it been as he said, it would have been كأنّها or كأنّهن; moreover, the pits have not been mentioned before so as to be referred to by a pronoun. Moreover, the comparison to the people is more fitting, especially as it is the view of one whose word is taken as proof.

nahhas-irab:21-22.t: فَكَيْفَ كانَ عَذابِي وَنُذُرِ (21): i.e. how was My punishment of them for unbelief, and My warning you that what befell them may befall you? Abū Isḥāq said: نذر is the plural of نذير.

nahhas-irab:23-23.t: كَذَّبَتْ ثَمُودُ بِالنُّذُرِ (23): ثمود is not declined as a triptote because it is the name of the tribe; it may be declined fully as being the name of the clan (ḥayy).

nahhas-irab:24-24.t: فَقالُوا أَبَشَراً مِنَّا واحِداً نَتَّبِعُهُ: You put بشرا in the accusative by an implied verb, and the meaning is: "Shall we follow a single human being from among us, while we are a multitude?" إِنَّا إِذاً لَفِي ضَلالٍ وَسُعُرٍ: i.e. in confusion away from the straight path and taking a crooked course. إذن does not govern when the speech does not rest upon it. وَسُعُرٍ may be the plural of سعير, or a maṣdar (verbal noun) from their saying سعر الرجل when a man becomes rash and frenzied.

nahhas-irab:25-25.t: أَأُلْقِيَ الذِّكْرُ عَلَيْهِ مِنْ بَيْنِنا: an interrogative containing the sense of rebuke (tawqīf). بَلْ هُوَ كَذَّابٌ أَشِرٌ: The Kufans say «بل» only comes after a negation, so they interpret the like of this according to the meaning, because the meaning of "was the Reminder sent down upon him?" is "it was not sent down upon him."

nahhas-irab:26-27.t:
سَيَعْلَمُونَ غَداً: The origin [of غد] according to Sībawayh is غدو; the wāw was dropped from it. مَنِ الْكَذَّابُ الْأَشِرُ: a mubtadaʾ (subject) and its khabar (predicate), [the clause being] in the position of the accusative governed by سيعلمون. Yaḥyā ibn Waththāb, al-Aʿmash and Ḥamza read it as ستعلمون غدا ("you will know tomorrow"), while Abū ʿUbayd inclines to the reading with yāʾ because after it comes إِنَّا مُرْسِلُوا النَّاقَةِ فِتْنَةً لَهُمْ, and He did not say "for you" (لكم). Abū Jaʿfar said: The implied construction for whoever reads with yāʾ is: Allah, Majestic and Mighty, said: سَيَعْلَمُونَ غَداً [Translator's note: so in the printed text; since the discussion answers the objection to the tāʾ reading, the intended sense may be the reading with tāʾ, with an implied "saying" before the second-person address], and "saying" is frequently omitted.

The origin is إنّا مرسلون; the nūn was dropped for lightness and [مرسلو] was put in construct [with الناقة]. فتنة لهم: Abū Isḥāq said: فتنة is a mafʿūl lahu (object of purpose). Someone else said: it is a maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. We tried them with that and tested them. Their trial in it was that the she-camel came out for them from a solid rock — a huge she-camel — and some of them believed. Because of her size she ate a great deal, so they complained of that to Ṣāliḥ ﷺ and said: "She has finished off the grasses and herbs and kept us from the water." He said: "Leave her to eat in Allah's earth and do not touch her with harm; she comes to the water one day and you come to it one day." This was the trial.

فَارْتَقِبْهُمْ وَاصْطَبِرْ: i.e. be patient in your watching for them. The origin is واصتبر; ṭāʾ was substituted for the tāʾ because ṭāʾ is more similar to ṣād, since both are emphatic (muṭbaq) letters. Abū Isḥāq said: the palate closes over the tongue with both of them. He also said: and they are both also "closed" (muṭbaq) in the script.

nahhas-irab:28-28.t: وَنَبِّئْهُمْ أَنَّ الْماءَ قِسْمَةٌ بَيْنَهُمْ: i.e. something subject to division (dhū qisma), like your saying "a man [who is] justice" (رجل عدل). كُلُّ شِرْبٍ مُحْتَضَرٌ: a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate); i.e. the she-camel comes [to the water] one day and they one day. The masculine was given precedence over the feminine, so it was said بينهم.

nahhas-irab:29-29.t:
فَنادَوْا صاحِبَهُمْ: They were the nine who took it on themselves alone to hamstring the she-camel; eight of them called Qudār and said: "Here is the she-camel; she has come." فَتَعاطى فَعَقَرَ: It was said: i.e. he undertook to kill her. Its true meaning in the language is: he reached for the she-camel and killed her, from their saying عطوت when you reach for something, as [the poet] said: [ṭawīl metre] 444-
وتعطو برخص غير شثن كأنّه ... أساريع ظبي أو مساويك إسحل
(She reaches out with soft, not coarse, [fingers], as though they were the worms of Ẓaby or tooth-sticks of isḥil wood.)

nahhas-irab:30-30.t: فَكَيْفَ كانَ عَذابِي: i.e. My punishment of them for their disobedience; i.e. so beware of acts of disobedience. وَنُذُرِ: i.e. My warning you that what befell them may befall you.

nahhas-irab:31-31.t:
This is among the wonderful similitudes, because al-hashīm is whatever of the trees has dried and been crushed, so that it is used to make an enclosure (yuḥẓar bihi) after having been green and fresh; i.e. after the blessing they became crumbled remains, and after the splendour, chaff like the condition of [dried] trees. It is related from Ibn ʿAbbās: «كهشيم المحتظر», i.e. like burnt bones. Abū Jaʿfar said:
The true meaning of this view in the language is: like dry stalks that have been used for an enclosure and burnt. Ibn Zayd said: it is the thorns that the Arabs put around the sheep for fear of wild beasts. The implied construction in Arabic is: like the dry stalks of the man who makes an enclosure (al-muḥtaẓir); and whoever reads كَهَشِيمِ الْمُحْتَظِرِ [Translator's note: the variant intended here is presumably المحتظَر with fatḥa, "the enclosed"; the vowelling has been lost in the printed text], its implied form is: like the dry stalks of the thing that has been enclosed.

nahhas-irab:33-33.t: i.e. the signs with which they had been warned.

nahhas-irab:34-34.t:
إِنَّا أَرْسَلْنا عَلَيْهِمْ حاصِباً: i.e. stones pelting them. إِلَّا آلَ لُوطٍ: accusative as the excepted (exception). The āl of a man is everyone who follows his religion and his way, as He, Majestic and Mighty, said to Noah ﷺ: إِنَّهُ لَيْسَ مِنْ أَهْلِكَ [Hūd: 46], although he was his son. آل and أهل mean the same, except that the grammarians say: the origin of آل is أهل, and the evidence for that is that when the Arabs make آل a diminutive they say أهيل.

نَجَّيْناهُمْ بِسَحَرٍ: al-Farrāʾ said: سحر here is fully declined because it is indefinite, like your saying "We saved them by night (بليل)." Abū Jaʿfar said: This is the view of all the grammarians; we know of no disagreement about it, except that after it he said something in which he dissents. He said: "When the Arabs drop the bāʾ from سحر they do not decline it fully, saying: فعلت هذا سحر يا هذا (I did this at dawn, you there)." [Translator's note: the printed text has سمر here; سحر is evidently intended.] Abū Jaʿfar said: The view of the Basrans is that سحر, when indefinite, is fully declined, and when definite is not, and the presence or absence of the bāʾ is the same. The reason for it according to Sībawayh is that it is diverted (maʿdūl) from [the form with] the alif and lām, because one says أتيتك أعلى السّحر (I came to you at the top of the dawn); so when the alif and lām were dropped while they were still intended, it became defective and was not fully declined. You say: سير بزيد سحر يا هذا ("Zayd was taken travelling at dawn, you there"), not fully declined. It is not permissible to put it in the nominative, for a reason which this is not the place to mention.

nahhas-irab:35-35.t: نِعْمَةً مِنْ عِنْدِنا: Abū Isḥāq said: You put نعمة in the accusative because it is a mafʿūl lahā (object of purpose). He said: the nominative is also permissible in the sense of "that is a blessing from Us." كَذلِكَ نَجْزِي مَنْ شَكَرَ: The kāf is in the position of the accusative, i.e. We reward whoever is thankful with a reward like that deliverance.

nahhas-irab:36-36.t: وَلَقَدْ أَنْذَرَهُمْ بَطْشَتَنا: i.e. [Our seizure] with which We seized them. فَتَمارَوْا بِالنُّذُرِ: i.e. they denied them out of doubt, as Qatāda said about فَتَمارَوْا بِالنُّذُرِ: i.e. they did not believe them.

nahhas-irab:37-37.t:
وَلَقَدْ راوَدُوهُ عَنْ ضَيْفِهِ فَطَمَسْنا أَعْيُنَهُمْ فَذُوقُوا عَذابِي وَنُذُرِ (37) وَلَقَدْ راوَدُوهُ عَنْ ضَيْفِهِ: «ضيف» has the meaning of "guests" (أضياف) because it is a maṣdar (verbal noun); that is why the Arabs hardly ever put it in the dual or plural. Its true sense in Arabic is: "concerning those who were his guests" (عن ذوي ضيفه). فَطَمَسْنا أَعْيُنَهُمْ: One says طمس عينه and طمس على عينه when he does something to it that makes it like [the rest of] his face, with no slit in it. And one says طمست الريح الأعلام when the wind has blown dust over the waymarks and covered them with it, as [the poet] said: [basīṭ metre] 445-
من كلّ نضّاخة الذّفرى إذا عرقت ... عارضها طامس الأعلام مجهول
(Of every she-camel whose nape gushes when she sweats, her track crossing [a desert] whose waymarks are effaced and unknown.)
فَذُوقُوا عَذابِي وَنُذُرِ: i.e. the angels, peace be upon them both [Translator's note: so in the text, «عليهما السلام», dual], said to them: "Taste the punishment of Allah and His penalty, of which He warned you."

nahhas-irab:38-40.t: Sufyān said: [بكرة means] it was with the dawn. بكرة is fully declined here because it is indefinite. al-Farrāʾ claimed that غدوة and بكرة are [both] declined fully and not declined fully, and claimed that more commonly غدوة is not fully declined and بكرة is fully declined. Abū Jaʿfar said: The view of the Basrans is that both are not fully declined when definite and are fully declined when indefinite. If someone were to claim that al-Farrāʾ's view is preferable because بكرة here is fully declined, it would be said to him: this does not follow, because بكرة here is indefinite, and likewise سحر. The evidence for that is that He did not say "they were destroyed on such a day of such a month of such a year, at dawn," which would make it definite. So since it must be indefinite, there is no proof in it, especially as it has the hāʾ [of the feminine]. عَذابٌ مُسْتَقِرٌّ: it was said: i.e. it settled upon them until it destroyed them.

nahhas-irab:41-41.t: i.e. the people of his religion and those who held his doctrine, as has passed. «قد», when it occurs with the past tense, indicates expectation, and when it is with the imperfect it indicates rarity; we say قد يكرمنا فلان, i.e. that rarely comes from him.

nahhas-irab:42-42.t: كَذَّبُوا بِآياتِنا كُلِّها: There are two views on its meaning. One of them is that the meaning is: they denied all of Our signs which We showed them. The other is that it is for expressing multitude, as Sībawayh reported: ما بقي منهم مخبّر ("not one of them was left to tell the tale"). فَأَخَذْناهُمْ أَخْذَ عَزِيزٍ مُقْتَدِرٍ: Qatāda said: Mighty in His vengeance. Someone else said to me: Mighty, not to be overcome; Able to do whatever He wills.

nahhas-irab:43-43.t: أَكُفَّارُكُمْ خَيْرٌ مِنْ أُولئِكُمْ: a mubtadaʾ (subject) and its khabar (predicate). He said: this is by way of rebuke (tawqīf), as Sībawayh reported: "Is misery dearer to you, or happiness?" أَمْ لَكُمْ بَراءَةٌ فِي الزُّبُرِ: i.e. or has it been written for you that you will not be punished?

nahhas-irab:44-44.t: [It is singular] according to the wording; had it been according to the meaning, it would have been said منتصرون.

nahhas-irab:45-45.t: سَيُهْزَمُ الْجَمْعُ: The people of tafsīr said: that was the day of Badr. وَيُوَلُّونَ الدُّبُرَ: a singular in the sense of the plural, as one says كثر الدّرهم ("the dirham has become plentiful").

nahhas-irab:46-46.t: بَلِ السَّاعَةُ مَوْعِدُهُمْ: Whoever says that «بل» only comes after a negation says: the meaning is: the matter is not as they say, that they will not be resurrected; rather the Hour is their appointment. وَالسَّاعَةُ أَدْهى وَأَمَرُّ: i.e. than their defeat and their turning back.

nahhas-irab:47-47.t: إِنَّ الْمُجْرِمِينَ فِي ضَلالٍ: i.e. departing from the truth. وَسُعُرٍ: i.e. a blazing fire.

nahhas-irab:48-48.t: يَوْمَ يُسْحَبُونَ فِي النَّارِ عَلى وُجُوهِهِمْ: In the reading of Ibn Masʿūd [it is] إلى النار ("to the Fire"), and this reading is by way of explanation, as Abū Hurayra related from the Prophet ﷺ [Translator's note: the text has only «صلّى الله عليه», the formula being abbreviated]: "The slain man will be brought before Allah, Majestic and Mighty, and He will say to him: 'For what were you killed?' He will say: 'For You.' He will say: 'You lie; you wanted it to be said: so-and-so is brave, and it has been said.' Then he will be ordered to be dragged on his face to the Fire." ذُوقُوا مَسَّ سَقَرَ: i.e. it will be said to them.

nahhas-irab:49-49.t: So by this He indicated that they are punished for their unbelief in the decree (al-qadar). Sībawayh claimed that the accusative of «كلّ» is according to the dialect of those who say زيدا ضربته ("Zayd, I struck him"). There are two other views on its accusative. As for the Kufans, they said: «إنّا» calls for a verb, and a verb is more appropriate to it than a noun; the meaning is: indeed We created everything. They said: this is not like our saying زيدا ضربته, because here there is no particle that is more appropriate to a verb. Do you not see that you say أزيدا ضربته, and the accusative is preferable, because here there is a particle that is more appropriate to a verb? The third view is that this was permitted in the accusative, differing from زيد ضربته, so as to indicate the creation of [all] things, so that there is in it a refutation of whoever denies the creation of acts.

nahhas-irab:50-50.t: وَما أَمْرُنا إِلَّا واحِدَةٌ: a mubtadaʾ (subject) and its khabar (predicate). ʿAlī ibn Sulaymān [al-Akhfash the Younger] said: the meaning is "except a single command." al-Farrāʾ claimed that وَما أَمْرُنا إِلَّا واحِدَةٌ was related in the accusative [i.e. واحدةً], as one says ما فلان إلّا ثيابه ودابّته ("so-and-so is nothing but his clothes and his mount"), i.e. he does nothing but look after his clothes and his mount; and as al-Kisāʾī reported: ما فلان إلّا عمّته ("so-and-so is nothing but his turban"), i.e. he looks after his turban. كَلَمْحٍ بِالْبَصَرِ: i.e. in its swiftness.

nahhas-irab:51-51.t: There are two views on it. One of them is that "their like" (أشياعهم) are those who were destroyed before them, because they disbelieved as these disbelieved; so is there anyone who takes admonition from that? They were called their like because they denied as these denied. The other view is that "their like" are those who used to help them in their enmity to the Prophet ﷺ and the believers, and they were destroyed; so is there anyone among you who takes admonition from that? The first view is the one held by the people of interpretation (taʾwīl).

nahhas-irab:52-52.t: The hāʾ in فعلوه refers back to the "likes" (al-ashyāʿ). في الزبر: written against them; the recording angels have written it.

nahhas-irab:53-53.t: One says سطر and استطر when someone writes a line.

nahhas-irab:54-54.t:
إِنَّ الْمُتَّقِينَ: i.e. those who guarded against the punishment of Allah, Majestic and Mighty, by avoiding what He has forbidden and performing what He has made obligatory. فِي جَنَّاتٍ وَنَهَرٍ: Abū Isḥāq said: «نهر» has the meaning of "rivers" (أنهار). Abū Jaʿfar said: al-Khalīl and Sībawayh recited: [rajaz metre] 446-
في حلقكم عظم وقد شجينا
(In your throat is a bone, and we have choked — i.e. "throat" singular for "throats".)

nahhas-irab:55-55.t: فِي مَقْعَدِ صِدْقٍ: i.e. in a seat of truth in which there is no idle talk and no falsehood. عِنْدَ مَلِيكٍ مُقْتَدِرٍ: i.e. who is able to do whatever He wills.

nahhas-irab:1-1.t: اقْتَرَبَتِ السَّاعَةُ: the tāʾ was given a kasra because of the meeting of two vowelless letters; and the tāʾ had to be vowelless because it is a particle that has come for a meaning. This is the view of the Basrans. As for the view of the Kufans, it is that since the tāʾs are four, the tāʾ of the speaker was given a ḍamma, the tāʾ of the masculine addressee a fatḥa, and the tāʾ of the feminine addressee a kasra, so no vowel remained, and the tāʾ of the absent feminine was made vowelless. [Translator's note: the source has «تاء المخاطب» for the first, evidently meaning the tāʾ of the speaker (al-mutakallim), as rendered.] The meaning is: the Hour in which the Resurrection will take place has drawn near, so beware of it, lest it come upon you suddenly while you persist in sins. وَانْشَقَّ الْقَمَرُ is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to اقتربت; its meaning is "the shining one".

nahhas-irab:2-2.t: وَإِنْ يَرَوْا آيَةً يُعْرِضُوا is a condition and its apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ). The meaning is that they asked for a sign, and were shown the moon split; so they saw a sign pointing to the truth of the Prophet's ﷺ affair and that what he brought is true, yet they turned away from affirming [it]. وَيَقُولُوا سِحْرٌ مُسْتَمِرٌّ: with an implied mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. "this is continuous magic".

nahhas-irab:3-3.t: وَكَذَّبُوا وَاتَّبَعُوا أَهْواءَهُمْ, i.e. they denied the reality of what they had seen and been certain of, and preferred following their desires in worshipping idols and abandoning what Allah commanded them. [وَكُلُّ] أَمْرٍ مُسْتَقِرٌّ is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate). The meaning is: every matter, good or evil, its settling is settled and its end is reached.

nahhas-irab:4-4.t: I.e. there has come to these polytheists, of the reports of the nations who did as they did and were destroyed, that which contains a restraint from what they are upon, as Mujāhid said: مزدجر means "restraint". The original form according to Sībawayh is مزتجر with tāʾ, except that the tāʾ is voiceless (mahmūs) and the zāy voiced (majhūr), so combining them was heavy, and the tāʾ was replaced with what is of its place of articulation, namely the dāl. Abū Jaʿfar said: This is among the most concise and subtle of his statements.

nahhas-irab:5-6.t: حِكْمَةٌ is a badal (substitute) from «ما», and the implied form is "and there has come to them wisdom", بالِغَةٌ, i.e. in which there is no deficiency. حكمة may also be nominative with an implied mubtadaʾ (subject). فَما تُغْنِ النُّذُرُ: «ما» may be in the position of the accusative by تغني, and the implied form is "so what do the warnings avail the one who has followed his desire and opposed the truth?"; and ما may be negative, with no position [in iʿrāb]. Some claimed that the yāʾ was dropped from تغن in the main text (al-sawād) because «ما» was treated like «لم». Abū Jaʿfar said: This is an ugly error, because «ما» is not one of the particles of the jussive; it falls on nouns and verbs, so it is impossible for it to put [a verb] in the jussive; and their meanings also differ, because «لم» makes the imperfect past, while «ما» negates the present. As for the dropping of the yāʾ from «تغن» in the main text, it follows the pronunciation in continuous speech (al-idrāj); and similar to it is يوم يدع الداعي إلى شيء نكر, written without wāw according to the pronunciation in continuous speech. As for الداعي when the yāʾ is dropped from it, what is said about it is that it is constructed on its indefinite [form]. What is clear [i.e. preferable] is that all this should be written without dropping.

nahhas-irab:7-8.t: خُشَّعاً is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial). أَبْصارُهُمْ is nominative by its verb[-like adjective]. This is the reading of the people of the two Sanctuaries; the people of Kufa and the people of Basra read «خاشعا أبصارهم», and from Ibn Masʿūd «خاشعة أبصارهم». Whoever says خاشعا makes it singular, because it is in the status of a verb that precedes [its agent]; whoever says خاشعة makes it feminine, like the feminine of a group; and whoever says خشّعا makes it plural, because it is a broken plural, and so it differs from the verb. Were it outside the Qur'an, the nominative would be permissible, by way of fronting and postponing. يَخْرُجُونَ is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl too. مِنَ الْأَجْداثِ: its singular is جدث, and جدف is also said for the grave, like فوم and ثوم. كَأَنَّهُمْ جَرادٌ مُنْتَشِرٌ is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl, and likewise His saying: مُهْطِعِينَ إِلَى الدَّاعِ. يَقُولُ الْكافِرُونَ هذا يَوْمٌ عَسِرٌ is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and its khabar (predicate).

nahhas-irab:9-9.t: كَذَّبَتْ قَبْلَهُمْ قَوْمُ نُوحٍ: according to the feminine of the collective. فَكَذَّبُوا عَبْدَنا, meaning Nūḥ. وَقالُوا مَجْنُونٌ: with an implied mubtadaʾ (subject). وَازْدُجِرَ, i.e. he was rebuked and threatened by their saying: "If you do not desist, we shall surely stone you."

nahhas-irab:10-10.t: فَدَعا رَبَّهُ أَنِّي مَغْلُوبٌ, i.e. "[saying] that I have been overcome and subdued". ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar read فَدَعا رَبَّهُ أَنِّي مَغْلُوبٌ with a kasra on the hamza. [Translator's note: the variant is printed identically to the standard reading; it is إِنِّي.] Sībawayh said: i.e. he said: "I am overcome." فَانْتَصِرْ, i.e. for me, by Your punishing them.

nahhas-irab:11-11.t:
فَفَتَحْنا أَبْوابَ السَّماءِ: the implied form is "so We helped him, and opened the gates of heaven", because what is apparent in the speech indicates what has been omitted. بِماءٍ مُنْهَمِرٍ, i.e. gushing. Sufyān said: منهمر means pouring forth in torrents. And the poet said [in the ramal metre]: 442-
راح تمريه الصّبا ثم انتحى ... فيه شؤبوب جنوب منهمر
(It set off in the evening, the east wind drawing [rain] from it; then there turned upon it a pouring downpour of the south wind.)

nahhas-irab:12-12.t:
وَفَجَّرْنَا الْأَرْضَ عُيُوناً: [عيون] is the plural of عين in number [i.e. of the multiplicity pattern]; the reading of the Kufans is عُيُوناً with a kasra on the ʿayn. [Translator's note: printed with ḍamma, identical to the standard; the Kufan reading meant is عِيُوناً.] The original is the ḍamma, and the ḍamma was replaced by a kasra, because combining a ḍamma and a yāʾ is felt to be heavy. فَالْتَقَى الْماءُ: التقى can only be of two [things]; the meaning is "so the water of the earth and the water of the heaven met", and both of them together are called ماء, because ماء is a generic noun. Abū al-Ḥasan ibn Kaysān said: the original of ماء is ماه; they replaced the hāʾ with a hamza, and when they make the plural they restore it to its original and say أمواه and مياه, and مويه in the diminutive. عَلى أَمْرٍ قَدْ قُدِرَ: it was said:
i.e. Allah, Majestic and Mighty, decreed it in the Preserved Tablet. And it was said: the water of the earth was measured to be like the water of the heaven.

nahhas-irab:13-13.t: وَحَمَلْناهُ عَلى ذاتِ أَلْواحٍ, i.e. on a ship made of planks. وَدُسُرٍ: Ibn Abī Ṭalḥa related from Ibn ʿAbbās; he said: الدّسر are the nails; and Muḥammad ibn Kaʿb, Qatāda and Ibn Zayd said the same. Al-Ḥasan said: الدّسر is the prow of the ship. Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: الدّسر is the edge of the ship. He said: the origin of this is from "دسره يدسره ويدسره دسرا" when he fastens it and pushes it.

nahhas-irab:14-14.t: تَجْرِي بِأَعْيُنِنا, i.e. within Our sight and hearing; and it was said: by Our command. أعين is a plural of paucity; one also says أعيان, like بيت and أبيات. جَزاءً is a maṣdar (verbal noun). لِمَنْ كانَ كُفِرَ: there are several views on its meaning. Ibn Zayd said: «من» is in the sense of «ما», and its implied form according to him is "for what was disbelieved of the blessings and denied". He said: and all the people of Arabic forbid this. The school of Mujāhid is that the meaning is "a recompense for Allah". Abū Jaʿfar said: This is a good view, i.e. "We punished them and [drowned] them as a recompense for Allah, Majestic and Mighty, when they disbelieved in Him and denied His oneness, saying: Do not abandon your gods, do not abandon Wadd nor Suwāʿ". [Translator's note: the source has «وعرفناهم», probably a misprint for «وغرّقناهم» "and We drowned them", which is how it is rendered.] And it was said: "a recompense for whoever disbelieved", according to the wording of «من»; and were it outside the Qur'an, on this view كفروا (plural) would be permissible according to the meaning.

nahhas-irab:15-15.t:
وَلَقَدْ تَرَكْناها آيَةً: it was said: the meaning is "and We left this punishment as an admonition and lesson for whoever disbelieves and denies the prophets ﷺ". The school of Qatāda: and We left the ship as a sign. فَهَلْ مِنْ مُدَّكِرٍ: this is the reading of the majority, and it is soundly reported from the Prophet ﷺ, as Shuʿba and others related from Ibn Isḥāq from al-Aswad from ʿAbd Allāh; he said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ recite فَهَلْ مِنْ مُدَّكِرٍ with the undotted dāl. Yaʿqūb the reader said: Qatāda read «فهل من مذّكر» with the dotted dhāl. Abū Jaʿfar said:
مدّكر is more fitting, because of the agreement we have mentioned and [because of] Arabic. The original form according to Sībawayh is مذتكر: the dhāl, which is voiced and radical, and the tāʾ, which is voiceless and augment, came together, so they replaced the tāʾ with a voiced letter from its place of articulation, and it became مذدكر; then the dhāl was assimilated into the dāl, and it became مدّكر. Whoever says مذّكر assimilated the dāl into the dhāl, and the speech of the Arabs is not according to this; they only assimilate the first into the second.

nahhas-irab:16-16.t: I.e. so how was My punishment of those who disbelieved in Me and disobeyed Me, and [how were] My warning and My cautioning against falling into the like of that?

nahhas-irab:17-17.t:
وَلَقَدْ يَسَّرْنَا الْقُرْآنَ لِلذِّكْرِ: Ibn Zayd said: i.e. We made it clear. Mujāhid said: We made it easy. And it was said:
the implied form is "and We have made the Qur'an easy, by Our clarifying it and setting it out in detail, for whoever wants to remember it and take a lesson from it". فَهَلْ مِنْ مُدَّكِرٍ who will remember what is in it? And it was said: is there anyone seeking good or knowledge, so that he may be helped to it? This is close to the first, but the first is clearer according to the apparent sense of the verse.

nahhas-irab:18-18.t: كَذَّبَتْ عادٌ: Abū Jaʿfar said: In this there is an omission whose meaning is known, i.e. ʿĀd denied Hūd as Quraysh denied Muḥammad ﷺ, so let them beware of the like of what befell them. فَكَيْفَ كانَ عَذابِي وَنُذُرِ: «فكيف» is in the position of the accusative as the khabar (predicate) of كان, except that it is indeclinable (mabnī), because it contains the meaning of interrogation; and it was given a fatḥa because of the meeting of two vowelless letters.
